sections.html:
Mason City is the county seat of Cerro Gordo County in north-central Iowa, about 120 miles north of Des Moines and 135 miles south of Minneapolis and Saint Paul. It sits on the Winnebago River at about 1,125 feet of elevation, with Clear Lake roughly 8 miles to the west.

Locals call it River City. The ZIP codes are 50401, 50402 and 50467, and the area code is 641. The street grid is split by Federal Avenue: east-side streets carry state names and west-side streets carry presidents' names, which makes an address easy to place.

The first settlers arrived in 1853 from LaSalle, Illinois, and the Masonic ties of one of them led to the name Masonic Grove. A town platted in 1854 was first called Shibboleth, then Masonville, and in 1855 it became Mason City to avoid confusion with another Masonville in Delaware County.

Cerro Gordo County organized its government in 1855. The General Assembly voted in 1856 to move the seat toward Clear Lake, but voters rejected the move in April 1858, and the seat has stayed in Mason City ever since. The railroad arrived in 1869 and the town was incorporated in 1870 with Darius B. Mason as its first mayor.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers show for Mason City housing?
sections.html:
Mason City had 27,338 residents in the 2020 census and the Census Bureau estimates 26,853 as of July 1, 2025. The city peaked at 30,642 in 1960, so it has lost population over six decades.

At 2.07 people per household, Mason City has many small households, and the median age in 2020 was 42.7. Those numbers fit a city where many owners are older and may be thinking about downsizing or leaving a house to heirs.

sections.h2: What drives the Mason City economy?
sections.html:
Healthcare is the largest sector: MercyOne North Iowa Medical Center employs over 2,000 people and has more than 400 medical providers. Retail, education and manufacturing round out the main sectors.

The city's older industries were brick, drain tile, limestone and cement. Until about 1934, Iowa produced more drain tile than any area its size, and Mason City was at the center of that output. A Heidelberg Materials cement plant still operates, while a Holcim plant is idle.

  • Curries, a door manufacturer owned by Assa Abloy
  • Woodhardbor Cabinetry and Stellar Industries
  • Principal Financial and Cargill Kitchen Solutions
  • A Kraft Foods plant making refrigerated Jell-O pudding snacks
  • Walmart, Menards, Target and Hy-Vee

Within about 20 miles are McKesson, Winnebago Industries and Sukup Manufacturing, which widens the commuting pool for sellers' buyers. In 2025, the city opened Prairie Rock Trails, with a bike park on the former Decker Meatpacking Plant site.

sections.h2: What makes Mason City houses architecturally unusual?
sections.html:
Mason City has one of the largest collections of Prairie School buildings in the world. The Rock Crest and Rock Glen Historic District holds at least 32 houses and one commercial building from 1908 to 1922, and 17 of them are on the National Register of Historic Places. Designers include Walter Burley Griffin, Marion Mahony Griffin and Barry Byrne.

Frank Lloyd Wright designed the Dr. G.C. Stockman House in 1908, the first Prairie School home in Iowa, which was moved four blocks in 1989 to avoid demolition. He also designed the Park Inn Hotel and City National Bank. Outside those districts, the city has Victorian, Craftsman, Bungalow and Mayan Revival homes.

If you own a house in or near a historic district, check with the city before changing the exterior, and mention any historic status in your listing or offer discussion. An older, unusual house is hard to price from a standard comparable.

sections.h2: How did the 2008 flood change Mason City neighborhoods?
sections.html:
In June 2008 the Winnebago River reached a record crest of 18.72 feet and overtopped the levee system. The city later ran a voluntary buyout and bought 167 properties, with FEMA hazard mitigation money and HUD community development funds paying for it.

Most of the historic houses affected were in the East Park Place area, and five of the 22 individually eligible houses were moved. East Park Historic District was added to the National Register in 2014. Anyone selling near the river should know the flood history, and a buyer's lender may ask about flood insurance.

Weather in general matters here. The average January high is 24.2 degrees and the July high is 82.5. Annual snowfall averages 44.4 inches, more than the other central Iowa cities, and the record low is minus 32. A rare February tornado struck on February 23, 1977.

sections.h2: What schools, roads and transit serve Mason City?
sections.html:
The Mason City Community School District runs Harding, Hoover, Jefferson and Roosevelt elementaries, Lincoln Intermediate, John Adams Junior High and Mason City High School. North Iowa Area Community College, Iowa's first public two-year junior college, is in the city, and Newman Catholic and North Iowa Christian School are private options.

Iowa 122 and U.S. 65 serve the city, U.S. 18 bypasses it to the south, and Interstate 35 is about 8 miles west. Mason City Municipal Airport has United Airlines flights to Chicago O'Hare. Mason City Transit runs five fixed routes with fares starting at 50 cents, and Jefferson Lines connects to Minneapolis, Des Moines and Kansas City.

sections.h2: What do Cerro Gordo County recording and tax rules mean for a seller?
sections.html:
The Cerro Gordo County Recorder is at 220 N. Washington Avenue in Mason City, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The county calculates transfer tax at $1.60 per thousand with the first $500 exempt. The Recorder does not keep abstracts, and a replacement can be requested from Cerro Gordo Abstract Company at 641-423-1145.

The office cannot help prepare documents, so it recommends talking to an attorney about adding or removing a name on a deed. On the median value of $142,000, the illustration is $141,500 divided by $500, or 283 increments, times $0.80, for $226.40.

  • First half due September 1, delinquent October 1
  • Second half due March 1, delinquent April 1
  • Statements mailed in mid to late August
  • 1.5 percent penalty each month after the due date
  • Annual electronic tax sale on the third Monday in June

The Treasurer's number is 641-421-3127. The tax sale redemption rate is 2 percent per month with guaranteed funds.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of a Mason City house work?
sections.html:
You tell us about the house, we review the condition and the title, and if you accept an offer, a title company closes the sale with the deed and recording. No lender is involved, so no loan appraisal can delay it.

Mason City sellers often have older houses, and a cash buyer does not require the roof, plumbing or flood repairs to be done first. An offer reflects the repairs, so compare it with a listing's likely net after costs. We do not promise a price in advance, and you owe nothing if you decline.
